free_tier.stated: MoFrp promises a permanently free basic service; the free tier is a check-in traffic model, where signing in each day grants additional traffic. [translated]

egress.terms: No byte figure is published on the marketing pages: traffic is granted by a daily check-in whose amount the site does not state, and the detail sits behind the console login at console.mofrp.com.; ingress: udp

interface_detail: Web panel for tunnel config, a Go client with no dependencies, and a documented API at /api/v3/tunnels.
tooling: Go single-binary client on Windows/macOS/Linux/Docker, plus a documented REST API; wg-quick on the local box
chaining: If the check-in allowance is large enough it is the only email-registrable UDP path besides Feige.

limits.value: daily check-in traffic; amount not published

binding_note: No constraint can be named: the free allowance is not published, so neither the quota nor the shaper can be shown to bind first. A check-in-only model normally lands near a few GB per month, which would fail on volume.

identity_cost.detail: Not established. console.mofrp.com/login serves a password login and console.mofrp.com/register redirects to the same login page, so no field list was visible. The token 'email' is the shape most likely for a console of this kind and is not a reading; treat the gate as unknown until an account is attempted.

reliability_note: None established; the vendor states tunnels persist as long as the terms are kept.
confidence_note: The protocol stack and the free-service promise are documented, but every number that decides the verdict is behind a login, and the identity field is a shape rather than a reading. One account would settle the quota, the per-tunnel bandwidth, the external UDP port and the gate in one step.

evidence.proved: free service, protocol stack TCP/UDP/HTTP/HTTPS/Websocket/P2P, check-in traffic model, domestic and overseas nodes

notes: Chooses no number at all on the public pages, which is itself the finding: the whole commercial surface is the console. Listed as a candidate for a user to test with one throwaway account rather than dismissed.

extras.wg_detail: The site lists TCP / UDP / HTTP / HTTPS / Websocket / P2P as the protocol stack, so a WG datagram can ride a UDP tunnel. No WG config is issued.
extras.volume_stated: No byte figure is published on the marketing pages: traffic is granted by a daily check-in whose amount the site does not state, and the detail sits behind the console login at console.mofrp.com.
extras.transit_note: Vendor relays, domestic and overseas nodes.
